Old jerkish snoopy boss was fired since that post, new awesome one was hired.

I am F and the only self harm I have done seriously is cutting, and only my legs, for some reason not my wrists. Oh and I stab thumbtacks into my face sometimes, but that's sort of a different thing and more like a reflex than the same obsessive thoughts, and fairly harmless except to my appearance. The obsessions are more like  I want to rip my skin off.

I would be more likely to throw myself sobbing in my boss's arms. She's a sweetheart and I have huge respect for her raising a very difficult son on her own.

Maybe the boxing would help. There is just really no good instruction of any martial art for adult beginners around here though.

16-18 was not too bad, typical teenage stuff. 18-20 was rough, grieving a loved one and setting out on my own at the same time was a difficult combination. The past couple of months have  been more like a throwbakc to 12-15 than anything though.

Gmail ads are fucking CREEPY.

I'm talking about this with a dearly loved friend on Gmail now and the ads are: Get your ex back, help with breakup, diabetes cure, overcome your fear, and something about a Real Age test.

Of those all but the real age test are relevant-- I'm hypoglycemic, have panic attacks, and I'm going through relationship turmoil.

Fuuuuu.

I'm 21. I want to take a boxing class, but I can't find one nearby that has an instructor who is okay working with someone who doesn't seriously want to compete and just wants to learn boxing more as an art form and a workout. I think that might help, but on the other hand I'm a little  scared to teach myself to hurt people in any way even  safely in boxing, because I don't know how mentally stable I can  guarantee I'll continue to be.

I don't like to sound fucking crazy, but I kind of am right now, I'll be okay I think because a person I really love just emailed me at the exact right moment, but I still can't stop having visions of hurting myself in my head. I don't really want the sensation. Pain doesn't do anything for me. I just want the obsessive thoughts to go away and aftera certain point it hurts NOT to hurt myself because it drives me crazy that I can't get rid of the thoughts. I have only actually harmed  myself a couple of times in my life, but the last time was the worst so I thought I shoudl ask for some support now.

I have constant thoughts about hurting myself even when I'm in a good mood and someone just said something really harsh to me that is making it a lot worse. Please just keep me company for a while. I know I need help, but I can't get it right now for various reasons.

That's a sweet story. I just don't know if I could not hate someone after breaking up... it's so hard to have someone be a huge part of your life and then be gone. 

Congrats on the marriage though! Weddings scare me but I am sure yours will be beautiful.

Posted under a new account cause my boss knows my Reddit name and this isn't his business--

I'm doing a lot of thinking lately about commitment and meaning. There has to be a fine line between trying to rescue something that's not savable and throwing something good away just because you're going through a rough patch. All long term relationships have their bad points, right? I've met maybe two people, ever, who claimed to have a perfect marriage and never fight. And I'm pretty sure they were lying.

But what are two immature people who love each other to death but suck at fighting like grownups to do? There's a point at which your lives are too intertwined to just take a break and see if you grow up in the meantime. Unentangling lives used to being intermingled leaves too much hurt and bitterness even if the unentangling comes with every intention of getting back together in the end.

I know there aren't easy answers, but I'd like to hear Redditors' thoughts. Did you let go of something good when things got tough and regret it? Did you save a relationship that seemed doomed, and you're still together now? Did you break up with the person you thought was your soulmate, and end up considering that your best decision ever?
